title.narrative: SNV Amplifying Youth Enterprises and Trade in Zimbabwe (AYET) 2025-2028
SNV Amplifying Youth Enterprises and Trade in Zimbabwe (AYET) 2025-2028 - SNV ISK

description.narrative: SNV Amplifying Youth Enterprises and Trade in Zimbabwe (AYET) project seeks to improve youth livelihoods and prospects through supporting access to “green” employment, entrepreneurial and trade opportunities in agri-food, renewable energy and emerging sectors in Zimbabwe

SNV:s projekt Amplifying Youth Enterprises and Trade in Zimbabwe (AYET) syftar till att förbättra ungdomars försörjningsmöjligheter och framtidsutsikter genom att stödja tillgången till ”gröna” anställningar, entreprenörskap och handelsmöjligheter inom jordbruk och livsmedel, förnybar energi och andra framväxande sektorer i Zimbabwe

The overall goal of the AYET project is improved youth livelihoods and prospects, through green employment and entrepreneurial and trade opportunities in agri-food, renewable energy, and emerging sectors.
The key objectives of the project are:
1. Match young people to economic opportunities in their communities with an emphasis on trade, climate resilience, and market development, and increased financial inclusion.
2. Increase access to employment and entrepreneurial skills development opportunities.
3. Support young people and financial institutions to access and develop appropriate financial products and services.
4. Contribute to supporting the creation of an enabling environment for youth participation in business.
Over the duration of project, a total of 13,000 youth and women will be reached directly and 52,000 indirectly in Zimbabwe, through both Sida and SDC support, with 50% being female. The project emphasizes jobs that support climate mitigation and resilience.
By creating inclusive economic growth and sustainable livelihoods for un- and underemployed young women and men, the project will:
a) Aim for integrating of emerging youth and women-led enterprises into pockets of economic growth. This will be done by improving business development support for promising youth-led enterprises, helping young people to gain technical skills and productive assets, and linking promising youth entrepreneur groups to higher value and export markets.
b) Support profitable youth-led enterprises in agri-food systems to increase sustainable productivity and climate change resilience.
c) Work with strategic knowledge institutions, private companies, youth-focused CSOs and other ecosystem actors, to develop and promote trade, climate-smart products, digital solution, and innovative financial products. These will include both rural and urban youths and women in the geographic areas of Manicaland, Mashonaland East, Matabeleland South, Harare, and Bulawayo provinces.
